Introduction and meaning
Causing miscarriage. BNS restatement of IPC 312. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 312. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 88 is the rule on “Causing miscarriage”. The section provides that whoever voluntarily causes a woman with child to miscarry, shall, if such miscarriage be not caused in good faith for the purpose of saving the life of the woman, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both; and, if the woman be quick with child, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 88 exists so that “Causing miscarriage” has a closed legal test in Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Sexual offences, assault, marriage, miscarriage, and offences against the child — placed first among the offence chapters.

The provision in detail
88. Whoever voluntarily causes a woman with child to miscarry, shall, if such miscarriage be not caused in good faith for the purpose of saving the life of the woman, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both; and, if the woman be quick with child, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine

Essential ingredients
1. Whoever voluntarily causes a woman with child to miscarry, shall, if such miscarriage be not caused in good faith for the purpose of saving the life of the woman, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both; and, if the woman be quick with child, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine

Explanations
Explanation.—A woman who causes herself to miscarry, is within the meaning of this section

hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 88 (Causing miscarriage), Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) Whoever voluntarily causes a woman with child to miscarry, shall, if such miscarriage be not caused in good faith for the purpose of saving the life of the woman, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both; and, if the woman be quick with child, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine
Step 3 — Read every Explanation. An explanation is part of the section. Omitting it leaves the analysis incomplete and vulnerable to rebuttal.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 88 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.

learningObjectives: Master the offence of voluntarily causing miscarriage under BNS s. 88.
Analyze the distinction in punishment between a woman 'with child' (up to 3 years) and a woman 'quick with child' (up to 7 years).
Understand the statutory exception for acts done in good faith to save the life of the woman, and alignment with the Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 88 penalizes voluntarily causing a woman with child to miscarry, punishable with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both; and if the woman be quick with child, with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine, unless caused in good faith to save the life of the woman.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Criminalizes unlawful termination of pregnancy while recognizing life-saving medical necessity as a complete statutory exception.
statutoryFramework: Chapter V — Of Offences against Women and Children, BNS s. 88 (corresponding to IPC s. 312).
Basic tier: Causing miscarriage to a woman 'with child' — imprisonment up to three years, or fine, or both.
Aggravated tier: Causing miscarriage to a woman 'quick with child' — imprisonment up to seven years, and fine.
Exception: Miscarriage caused in good faith for the purpose of saving the life of the woman.
Explanation: A woman who causes herself to miscarry is within the meaning of this section.
Interplay with special statutes: Subject to the provisions of the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act, 1971.
essentialIngredients: The accused caused the woman to miscarry.
The miscarriage was NOT caused in good faith for the purpose of saving the life of the woman.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 88 criminalizes the non-therapeutic expulsion of the fetus. The law draws a crucial medical and legal distinction between a woman being 'with child' (simply pregnant, from conception onwards) and 'quick with child' (where fetal movement has become perceptible to the mother, typically around the fourth to fifth month). Causing miscarriage when quick with child attracts an aggravated punishment of up to seven years. The Explanation clarifies that a pregnant woman who takes substances or uses instruments on herself to cause miscarriage is equally liable under this section. The sole statutory exception within the section is an act done in good faith for saving the life of the mother. Lawful terminations conducted by registered medical practitioners in compliance with the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act are legally immune.
examples: Teaching example (Unlawful termination): An unqualified person administers abortifacient pills to a pregnant woman at her request to terminate a healthy five-month pregnancy without medical justification. The fetus was quick. Both the person administering and the woman are liable under s. 88 (aggravated tier).

Teaching example (Saving the life of the mother): A surgeon performs an emergency medical procedure on a woman experiencing severe internal hemorrhage and uterine rupture to save her life, resulting in termination of pregnancy. The surgeon is protected by the good-faith exception.
distinctions: Woman with child vs Quick with child: 'With child' means pregnant; 'quick with child' means advanced pregnancy where fetal movements are felt, attracting double the maximum penalty.

Section 88 vs Section 89: Section 88 contemplates miscarriage with or without consent (punishing up to 3 or 7 years); Section 89 specifically punishes causing miscarriage without the woman's consent with up to life imprisonment.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether a woman who consumed toxic herbal concoctions causing her own four-month pregnancy to abort is punishable under s. 88.
Rule: Under the Explanation to BNS s. 88, a woman who causes herself to miscarry is within the scope of the section.
Application: She acted voluntarily and the termination was not necessary to save her life.
Conclusion: She is liable under BNS s. 88.

Includes self-induced miscarriage by the pregnant woman herself.
Exception exists for acts done in good faith to save the mother's life.
